root_idea.summary: The root's semantic orientation is subjection or being held under constraint, with a parallel line of bringing something forth or making it manifest.
root_idea.development: The lexical field connects humility and captivity with restraint, coercive or surrendered taking, and the emergence or display of what is concealed. Naming or titling is also treated as an indication of something else; these are related developments, not a single meaning of every form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form عَنَا rather than the inflected Quranic form عَنَتِ.

senses.definition: To become lowly, humble, submissive, or obedient.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ, the faces—by extension, the persons—are humbled and submissive before God. The expression may evoke the submission of captives or the posture of prostration.

senses.definition: To suffer weariness, hardship, or toil.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative interpretation of the Quranic expression at 20:111, taking the form in connection with the sense of undergoing exertion or affliction rather than simply describing humility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become or remain a captive; to be confined in captivity, especially with hardship or humiliation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may describe remaining among people as a prisoner or being held fast in confinement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take possession of something by force; in another attested usage, to take it by peaceful surrender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two applications are explicitly reported as contrary usages of the same verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put forth or produce something, or to make it apparent or show it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of land bringing forth plants or herbage, and of something failing or succeeding to appear or be yielded to someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of events, to befall someone; of an affair, to prove difficult or distressing to him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical use covers both the occurrence of events and the resulting difficulty or trouble.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a dog, to come to a thing and smell it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the thing approached and sniffed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a waterskin, to fail to retain water and let it escape; of blood, to flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The waterskin usage emphasizes water appearing or leaking from the vessel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stand or rise to a standing position.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported additional verbal usage of the Form I stem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To imprison or confine someone for a long time, straitening him; to restrain or suppress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The restraining sense also applies to suppressing or checking voices and other outward activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smear a camel with عَنِيَّة, a medicinal preparation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is specifically the camel treatment called عَنِيَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render someone lowly, humble, or submissive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the causative Form IV counterpart of becoming lowly or submissive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone remain captive or stick fast in captivity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative construction places the person in, or keeps him in, confinement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of rain, to water land so that it produces vegetation; of a man, to find land with abundant pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two constructions describe either causing growth or encountering land whose growth and grazing are plentiful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become smeared with عَنِيَّة, the camel treatment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a camel treated with the preparation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a title or superscription on a book or writing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb also occurs with the meaning of writing the book's title or heading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A side, region, quarter, or tract of a country or of the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may refer to the sides of the face.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A party or group of people from different tribes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is another singular use associated with the plural أَعْنَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Force, constraint, or the taking of something by force.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe a city or possession taken through conflict and superior power.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Love or affection; submission or concession; or taking by peaceful surrender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is explicitly reported with usages contrary to the coercive sense, including surrender or concession motivated by affection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lowliness, humility, or submissiveness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or substantive associated with the Form I sense of becoming lowly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of captivity or confinement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the substantive use associated with becoming or remaining captive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of putting forth or producing something, or of making it apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This substantive use follows the corresponding Form I usages of bringing forth and showing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The title, superscription, or inscription of a book or writing; an address or heading.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: By extension, anything serving as an indication or identifying mark of another thing is an عُنْوَان, including a visible mark on the forehead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel preparation made chiefly from inspissated urine, sometimes mixed with dung or other substances, and used to treat mange or scab.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also be used for related tar-like or medicinal substances applied to affected camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lowly, humble, or submissive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is also associated with the condition of one held under another's power.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A captive or confined person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine and plural forms may be used for female captives or persons treated like captives.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Women in a condition of captivity or treated like captives.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is explained through confinement in the homes of their husbands or through being wronged without defense; the source presents these as explanations of the application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Workers or laborers; also, as a substantive application, the legs or limbs of riding beasts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same form is tentatively extended to collectors of imposts, understood as workers for oppressors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flowing, said of blood or water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing a liquid in motion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stallion camel of mean origin that is confined when excited by lust, or whose legs are bound for that purpose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The confinement prevents or avoids his use as a breeding or riding animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel deliberately disabled so that it cannot be ridden or otherwise used.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported practice involved displacing a vertebra's projections and wounding the hump when the owner's herd reached a specified number; its explanation is associated either with fatigue or confinement from free use.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the inflected form عَنَتِ, while the public citation headword is normalized to عَنَا. The verse has an alternative interpretation involving hardship or toil in addition to the primary sense of humility and submission.
